Greeneye Loader on Linux (Steam Deck, Proton, Wine)
====================================================

Windows players: you don't need anything in this file.

On Linux the loader can't run under its usual name, dbgcore.dll, because Wine never loads that
name. It runs as dinput8.dll instead. It's the same file, renamed.


1. Rename the loader
--------------------

In the game folder (the one with enshrouded.exe), or the server folder (the one with
enshrouded_server.exe):

    rename  dbgcore.dll  to  dinput8.dll

Keep the greeneye folder where it is.

This needs Greeneye Loader 1.2.4 or newer. Older copies don't have the functions a dinput8.dll
must have, so the game won't start with one renamed to dinput8.dll. Several mods ship the loader,
so take dbgcore.dll from your newest mod download. Once the game starts, the first line of
greeneye\loader.log shows the loader's version.

Already have a dinput8.dll from another mod (Creative Mode, XHL, ...)? Don't overwrite it. Do
step 3 first.


2. Tell Wine to use the dinput8.dll in the game folder
------------------------------------------------------

By default Wine uses its own dinput8.dll and ignores the one in the game folder. The setting
that changes that is:

    WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b"

"n,b" means native (the file in the game folder) first, then Wine's built-in one. Set it in
whichever of these places matches how you play.

Steam (Proton), desktop Linux or Steam Deck:
  1. In your Steam Library, right-click Enshrouded and choose Properties.
     (Steam Deck Game Mode: select Enshrouded, press the gear button, then Properties.)
  2. On the General page, find Launch Options and type exactly:

         WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b" %command%

  3. Close the window. Steam saves it right away.

  If Launch Options already has something in it, put the setting at the very front, and keep
  only one %command%:

      gamemoderun %command%
      becomes
      WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b" gamemoderun %command%

  If it already has a WINEDLLOVERRIDES, add dinput8 to the same one, separated by a semicolon:

      WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dxgi=n,b" %command%
      becomes
      WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dxgi=n,b;dinput8=n,b" %command%

Instead of launch options, you can set it once in the game's Proton prefix with winecfg
(Enshrouded's Steam app id is 1203620):

      protontricks 1203620 winecfg

  In winecfg, open the Libraries tab, type dinput8 under "New override for library", click
  Add, and make sure it reads "dinput8 (native, builtin)". Then click OK.

Lutris:
  Right-click the game > Configure > Runner options > DLL overrides. Add a row with key
  dinput8 and value n,b. Save.

Plain Wine (your own prefix):
  Either start the game with
      WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b" wine enshrouded.exe
  or run winecfg for that prefix and add the dinput8 override as described above.

Dedicated server under Wine (start script):
  Put this line in the script before the line that starts the server:
      export WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b"
  or put it in front of the start command:
      WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b" wine enshrouded_server.exe

Dedicated server in Docker (docker-compose.yml):
  Add it to the container's environment. No quotes in this form:
      environment:
        - WINEDLLOVERRIDES=dinput8=n,b
  With docker run:  -e WINEDLLOVERRIDES=dinput8=n,b
  If the image already sets WINEDLLOVERRIDES, add ;dinput8=n,b to its value instead.

Server panels (AMP, Pterodactyl, game hosts):
  Add an environment variable to the server's startup settings:
      name:   WINEDLLOVERRIDES
      value:  dinput8=n,b
  Not every host lets you set environment variables. If yours doesn't, ask their support to
  add it.


3. Already have another dinput8.dll mod? Chain it
-------------------------------------------------

Only one file can be called dinput8.dll. The loader can load the other mod for you:

  1. Rename the other mod's dinput8.dll to something else, e.g. creative.dll. Keep it in the
     game folder.
  2. Copy greeneye\linux\dinput8-chain.ini.example to the game folder as dinput8-chain.ini,
     and list that file under [Chain]:

         [Chain]
         creative.dll

  3. Put the loader in as dinput8.dll (step 1).

The loader loads every DLL listed under [Chain] when the game starts, before the game's own
code runs, which is about when the other mod would have loaded under its own name. EMF, Kiln,
ShroudForge, XHL and Auto Loot Plus read this same file the same way, so a dinput8-chain.ini you
already have keeps working, and yours keeps working if you switch loaders. DLLs that EMF's
installer moved into an [EMF] section are loaded too.

Put "; " in front of a line to switch that DLL off without deleting it. Only DLLs inside the
game folder count: write creative.dll or mods\mymod\mymod.dll, not a full path.

Chaining works on Windows too, if two of your mods want dinput8.dll. On Windows, though, the
simpler fix is to leave the loader as dbgcore.dll, where it doesn't need the name.

Don't list the Greeneye Loader itself (dbgcore.dll, or a copy under another name) under
[Chain]. It's already running as dinput8.dll, so it skips any copy of itself and says so in
loader.log.

Another loader, like XHL, already owns dinput8.dll and reads dinput8-chain.ini itself? Then you
can do it the other way round: leave that loader as dinput8.dll and list the Greeneye Loader
under its [Chain], renamed to something like greeneye-loader.dll (not dinput8.dll). Our mods
then start as soon as that loader loads it.


Both dbgcore.dll and dinput8.dll in the folder?
-----------------------------------------------

A mod update may put dbgcore.dll back next to your dinput8.dll. Nothing breaks:
  - On Linux, Wine never loads dbgcore.dll, so it just sits there. You can delete it.
  - On Windows, both load. One copy runs the mods, and the dinput8.dll copy still loads your
    chain. greeneye\loader.second-copy.log says which copy runs the mods; if that file says the
    idle copy is newer, replace the older file with the newer one.
When the dinput8.dll copy only loads the chain, its log is greeneye\loader.chain.log.


4. Check that it works
----------------------

Start the game or server once, then open greeneye\loader.log. The first line should read
something like:

    Greeneye Loader 1.2.4 loaded as DINPUT8.dll in enshrouded.exe (game), ... on Wine 9.0

No loader.log at all? Wine didn't use the game folder's dinput8.dll. Check the override
(step 2). On Steam, make sure %command% is in the launch options.

With a chain, loader.log also lists each chained DLL ("chain: creative.dll started") or
says why one was skipped.

If a mod or a chained DLL crashes the game while it starts, the loader skips it at the next
launches and says so in loader.log, until that DLL is updated. To try it again anyway, delete
greeneye\crashguard.txt.

When reporting a problem, please attach greeneye\loader.log.
